Hypotheses:
- nda-10: Confidentiality of Agreement | Receiving Party shall not disclose the fact that Agreement was agreed or negotiated.
- nda-4: Limited use | Receiving Party shall not use any Confidential Information for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement.
- nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure | Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or judicial process to disclose any Confidential Information.
- nda-12: Permissible development of similar information | Receiving Party may independently develop information similar to Confidential Information.
- nda-19: Survival of obligations | Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement.
- nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information | Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information.
- nda-16: Return of confidential information | Receiving Party shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement.
- nda-1: Explicit identification | All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party.
- nda-15: No licensing | Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information.
- nda-7: Sharing with third-parties | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some third-parties (including consultants, agents and professional advisors).
- nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession | Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information.
- nda-11: No reverse engineering | Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
- nda-17: Permissible copy | Receiving Party may create a copy of some Confidential Information in some circumstances.
- nda-13: Permissible acquirement of similar information | Receiving Party may acquire information similar to Confidential Information from a third party.
- nda-2: None-inclusion of non-technical information | Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
- nda-5: Sharing with employees | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some of Receiving Party's employees.
- nda-18: No solicitation | Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives.

Thought: Let me analyze each hypothesis against the document segments.

nda-10: Confidentiality of Agreement - The document doesn't mention keeping the Agreement's existence confidential. NotMentioned.

nda-4: Limited use - Segment [10] says "Recipient agrees not to use the Confidential Information in any way" - this restricts use. Combined with [5] stating the Purpose. Segment [10] says no use in any way, which entails limited use. Entailment with evidence [10] (and possibly [5]).

nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure - Segment [11] says Recipient must prevent disclosure "even if authorized or directed under any law, without the express permission of the Discloser." This doesn't say notify - it says get express permission. This is arguably contradiction or entailment? The hypothesis says "shall notify Disclosing Party in case required by law to disclose." The document says Recipient must not disclose even if required by law without express permission - this implies seeking permission, which is stronger than notice. Hmm, this could be Entailment (permission requirement implies notification) or NotMentioned. Actually requiring express permission before disclosure under law implies the Recipient must inform the Discloser. I'd lean Entailment with evidence [11]. But strictly, "notify" isn't stated. Many NDA datasets label this as Entailment if permission is required. Let me verify with human feedback.

nda-12: Permissible development of similar information - Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-19: Survival of obligations - Not mentioned explicitly. Segment [29] talks about term until termination. No survival clause. NotMentioned.

nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information - Segment [7] mentions information "provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing." Entailment with evidence [7].

nda-16: Return of confidential information - Not mentioned. Segment [14] says layout plan shall always be in custody of Discloser - that's not return upon termination. NotMentioned.

nda-1: Explicit identification - Segment [7] says "Confidential Information as identified and reduced in writing or provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing" - this suggests identification but also allows verbal/unwritten, contradicting "All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified." Hmm. The phrase "as identified" suggests identification requirement. But "or in any other way not reduced in writing" contradicts express identification of ALL information. This could be Contradiction. Actually the hypothesis: "All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party." The document allows information provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing - meaning not all is expressly identified in writing. But "identified" could be oral too. Ambiguous. The segment says "as identified and reduced in writing or provided verbally..." - the "as identified" may modify all. I'd say Entailment with [7]? Or Contradiction? In the NDA dataset (this looks like the ContractNLI dataset), nda-1 for this document... Let me think. The clause says information "as identified and reduced in writing or provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing at the time of such disclosure." This means CI includes info identified in writing OR provided verbally - so not all CI is expressly identified (in writing). That contradicts "All CI shall be expressly identified." Hmm, but "identified" could happen verbally. The typical ContractNLI label for such catch-all provisions is Contradiction for explicit identification. Actually in ContractNLI, "Explicit identification" is entailed when the agreement says CI must be marked/identified, and contradicted when it includes catch-all like "or information that should reasonably be considered confidential." Here, info "provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing" is a catch-all → Contradiction with evidence [7].

nda-15: No licensing - Not mentioned explicitly. NotMentioned.

nda-7: Sharing with third-parties - Segment [10] says no sharing with any Third Party. Contradiction with evidence [10].

nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession - Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-11: No reverse engineering - Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-17: Permissible copy - Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-13: Permissible acquirement of similar information - Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-2: None-inclusion of non-technical information - Segment [3] lists CI including "services, customers etc" - non-technical info included. Contradiction with evidence [3].

nda-5: Sharing with employees - Not mentioned. Segment [10] prohibits sharing with Third Party - employees of Recipient aren't third parties necessarily. NotMentioned.

nda-18: No solicitation - Not mentioned. NotMentioned.
